title: speculative-decode-early-exit-field-log-ansel
content:
Goal / hypothesis:

Quick notes to self while running the speculative decoding + early-exit patch on a small fleet. Hypothesis: combining a shallow speculative token generator (spec-factor=2) with an early-exit confidence threshold on the language head (conf_thresh=0.82) reduces p99 generation latency for short requests (<=40 tokens) without materially increasing cost or harming p50. Expectation: token throughput might increase slightly due to faster termination on many examples, but KV-cache churn could negate gains for multi-turn contexts.

Environment / baseline:
- Model: rw-open-7b-v2 (float16), same weights for all runs.
- Hardware: 4x A10G dedicated worker pool (single-model allocation per worker), 32GB host mem.
- Baseline runtime: greedy decode, no speculative, no early-exit (master at commit 4b9c).
- Traffic generator: local replay of 10k short conversational requests sampled from prod-sample-2024-10 (mixture: 70% single-turn Qs, 30% short chat turns).
- Metrics captured: latency token-at-a-time wallclock, p50/p95/p99 generation complete, tokens/sec, KV-cache hit ratio, retransmits (fallbacks), cost estimate per 1M tokens from billing model.

Key config knobs tested:
1) spec_factor {1 (none), 2, 3}  -- how many speculative tokens are proposed ahead of authoritative head
2) conf_thresh {0.70, 0.82, 0.90} -- early-exit confidence threshold when to stop decoding early
3) speculative_fallback_timeout_ms {0 (immediate fallback), 5, 10} -- how long to wait for authoritative check before accepting speculative tokens
4) kv_cache_prefetch {on|off} -- whether speculative proposals pre-warm KV cache for next step

Experiment matrix (summary runs):
- Run A (baseline): spec_factor=1, conf_thresh=N/A, fallback_timeout=0, kv_cache_prefetch=off
- Run B: spec_factor=2, conf_thresh=0.82, fallback_timeout=5ms, kv_cache_prefetch=on
- Run C: spec_factor=3, conf_thresh=0.70, fallback_timeout=10ms, kv_cache_prefetch=on
- Run D: spec_factor=2, conf_thresh=0.90, fallback_timeout=5ms, kv_cache_prefetch=off

Results (aggregated):
- Baseline (Run A): p50=28ms, p95=120ms, p99=280ms, tokens/s=780k, KV hit=96.1%, fallback_rate=0%
- Run B: p50=26ms, p95=98ms, p99=190ms, tokens/s=930k, KV hit=95.6%, fallback_rate=3.8%
- Run C: p50=25ms, p95=110ms, p99=220ms, tokens/s=1.02M, KV hit=94.2%, fallback_rate=9.7%
- Run D: p50=27ms, p95=105ms, p99=205ms, tokens/s=890k, KV hit=95.9%, fallback_rate=1.4%

Quick interpretation:
- Best p99 improvement seen in Run B (spec_factor=2 + conf_thresh=0.82 + kv prefetch). p99 dropped ~32% vs baseline.
- Run C (more aggressive spec) improved tokens/sec but fallback_rate jumped to ~10% which added jitter and increased KV churn; not acceptable for multi-turn chat where cache continuity matters.
- Run D (tight conf_thresh=0.90) reduces false accepts (fallback_rate 1.4%) but p99 improvement smaller than Run B — likely too conservative threshold.
- KV cache prefetching appears net-positive in this mix: lower p99 in B vs D even though fallback exists; prefetch warms next step and reduces miss penalty.

Observed failure modes / anomalies:
- Rare but visible double-token emission (client-side observable duplicate token) when speculative accepted and authoritative arrives late; caused edge-case in merging logic. Repro rate ~0.02% of requests on Run C.
- For requests with long contexts (>200 tokens) the speculative proposals caused >1% KV eviction events on a10g due to prefetch working set expansion; avoided by turning prefetch off for long-context requests.
- Small subset (approx 5% of prompts) where early-exit cut answers short and quality dropped (conf_thresh too aggressive). These are mostly factual/multi-step reasoning prompts — need safety bump or prompt-length aware threshold.

Micro-cost estimate (very rough):
- Baseline cost per 1M tokens (in this env): $58.
- Run B: +2.3% raw token costs due to some fallbacks -> net cost ~$59.3, but effective user-perceived latency improvement suggests better UX for interactive apps.
- Run C: +6.8% token cost because of higher retransmit rate despite throughput gains -> ~$62.9. Not worth it.

Quick ascii latency curve (p99 across runs)
( lower is better )
Run A [###########] 280ms
Run B [#######    ] 190ms
Run C [########  ] 220ms
Run D [########  ] 205ms

Actionable next steps / TODOs:
- Fix merge edge-case that causes duplicate token emission (high priority). Patch idea: sequence watermark + idempotent client emit suppression.
- Add 'context-length aware' heuristics: disable prefetch / reduce spec_factor when context_tokens > 128.
- Run a targeted quality evaluation on prompts requiring multi-step reasoning; set per-prompt conf threshold overrides (or opt-out tag).
- Add telemetry: label speculative-accepted vs authoritative pathways in traces so we can easily filter traces with fallbacks and duplicates.
- Run same matrix on a heterogeneous fleet (8xH100) to compare hardware impact; H100 may tolerate larger spec_factor with less KV churn.

Experiment artifacts / commands used (local):
- ./bench/replay.py --input samples/short-chat-10k.json --config experiments/speculative/bench-b.json --out results/b.json
- runtime PR with feature flag: feature/speculative-early-exit (see linked PR).

Notes to self:
- This is promising for low-latency single-turn UIs (search, chat bubbles). For long-form generation and chain-of-thought we must be conservative.
- When communicating to product: frame this as a latency-improvement mode with opt-in heuristics for conversation UIs; show cost tradeoffs.

References / saved traces: results/b.json, results/c.json (kept in my local sandbox).

End of log.

-- Ansel
